FXUS64 KFWD 011939
AFDFWD

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Fort Worth TX
239 PM CDT Sat Jul 1 2023

...New Long Term... 

.SHORT TERM... /Issued 1156 AM CDT Sat Jul 1 2023/
/This afternoon through Sunday/

Showers and storms that developed across the Big Country this
morning near a weak cold front continue to move into the western
zones late this morning. Considerable cloud cover and lower 
instability will neutralize the storms quickly as they move east 
across North Texas.

A well defined outflow has moved well out ahead of the storms and
will likely be a source for scattered afternoon convection across
parts of North and Central Texas. The best instability resides 
near and south of the I-20 corridor and this is also the region 
that has seen the least amount of cloud cover this morning, so we
will keep afternoon PoPs highest there. Storms will be possible 
through the evening, but a loss of surface heating and lack of 
large scale support will result in a decrease in coverage. Any 
storms that develop this afternoon will have a potential to 
produce gusty outflow winds and possibly small hail. 

Even though many areas will not see appreciable rainfall this
afternoon, extensive cloud cover will keep temperatures
considerably cooler than they have been in several days. We will 
lower afternoon highs in most locations with many of the western 
zones struggling to get out of the 80s (a great way to start 
July).

Sunday will remain unsettled with troughing in place aloft and
multiple outflow boundaries lingering across the region. We will
keep low chance PoPs (generally 20%-40%) for the entire forecast 
area. The good news is that the day will not be a washout anywhere
and plenty of cloud cover will keep afternoon highs near or even 
below normal in some locations. 

79

&&

.LONG TERM... /NEW/
Update:
No significant changes were made to the long term forecast.
Seasonably hot temperatures and daily diurnally driven rain/storm
chances will continue through most of the week, including through
the 4th of July holiday. While severe weather is not expected,
frequent lightning and gusty winds will be hazardous to those who
are outdoors.

Garcia

Previous Discussion:
/Sunday Night Onward/

Sunday afternoon convection will linger into the evening hours, 
but should dissipate by midnight with the loss of surface 
instability. A weak, positive tilt trough will linger overhead in 
the days that follow, leading to diurnally driven convection each 
afternoon through the middle of next week. Showers and storms will
be disorganized, and will likely initiate along mesoscale 
boundaries left over from activity in the preceding days. Pops 
each day will be in the chance to slight chance categories due to
the expectation of convection being isolated to scattered in 
nature. 

It still appears that Thursday may be one of our better 
opportunities to receive rain as a large scale trough sweeps 
through the Northern and Central Plains, and a pair of shortwaves
swing around its base. The initial shortwave will pass through 
the area during the day, generating the first round of scattered 
showers and storms. The best chances at this time look to be 
across the eastern half of the forecast area where the stronger 
lift will be. As these storms are exiting to the southeast, a 
second batch associated with the next shortwave will be 
approaching from the northwest Thursday evening. The best rain 
chances associated with the second shortwave will likely be along 
the Red River, with storms weakening the farther south they get. 
There is still a lot of uncertainty regarding exact timing and 
areal coverage, but we should be able to narrow it down as we get 
in range of higher resolution model guidance. As far as the 
severity of the convection each day, weak flow aloft will keep the
majority of the storms sub-severe, though isolated damaging wind 
gusts could occur in the stronger storms. 

Whatever the case, it looks like our rain chances will dwindle
Friday through next weekend as the mid level ridge moves in from
the west, regains control, and returns typical July Texas weather
to the region.

30
&&

.AVIATION... /Issued 1258 PM CDT Sat Jul 1 2023/
/18Z TAFs/

The primary aviation weather concern is thunderstorm timing as
well as any temporary wind shifts due to outflow boundaries.

Convection west of the Metroplex TAF sites will continue to 
weaken as it moves into slightly more stable air. However, there 
is enough instability to warrant the mention of thunder in the 
vicinity of all Metroplex terminals this afternoon. It appears 
that the better instability will reside just to the south along 
and ahead of a well defined outflow boundary (near a line from 
Goldthwaite to Hillsboro to Greenville at 1230 PM). The area 
south of the boundary has also seen the most sun today and will 
continue to destabilize through the afternoon. For now, we left 
thunder out of the Waco TAF but we will continue to monitor the 
progress of the outflow for future updates. Convective trends 
Sunday should be very similar to today with scattered storms 
during the heat of the day.

Otherwise, expect VFR with broken to overcast middle and high
clouds and few to scattered Cu.  

A west to northwest wind at the start of the TAF cycle at the
Metroplex terminals will become more southwest/south through the
afternoon once the outflow moves a bit farther south. Southerly
flow will continue overnight and Sunday outside of any convective
outflows that may develop. Prevailing wind speeds will remain 
generally below 12 knots. 

79

&&

.AVIATION...
/12z TAFs/

Southwest winds now prevail following a westerly wind shift 
overnight which was the result of convective outflow. Winds will 
likely oscillate between west and southwest through most of today,
with low chances for convective impacts at the airports during 
the early/mid afternoon time period. Following a lull in 
convective potential later in the evening/overnight period, 
additional scattered storms are possible heading into Sunday, but 
timing and coverage remain too uncertain to introduce any TS near 
the end of the valid TAF period. 

-Stalley
